# 1 Chronicles Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 382r–382v

---

**1** When David was old and had lived a full life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.

**2** He assembled all of Israel's leaders, along with the priests and Levites.

**3** The Levites who were thirty years old or older were counted. The total came to 38,000 men.

**4** David assigned them: "Of these, 24,000 will supervise the work of the LORD's house. 6,000 will serve as administrators and judges.

**5** 4,000 will be gatekeepers, and 4,000 will worship the LORD with musical instruments — instruments I designed for that purpose."

**6** David organized them into divisions based on the three branches of Levi's family: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

**7** From the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.

**8** Ladan's sons: Jehiel (the leader), Zetham, and Joel — three in all.

**9** Shimei's sons: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran — three. These were the family heads under Ladan.

**10** Shimei also had sons: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah — four.

**11** Jahath was the leader, Zizah second. Jeush and Beriah did not have many descendants, so they were counted together as a single family unit.

**12** Kohath's sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel — four.

**13** Amram's sons: Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were permanently set apart for the most sacred duties — to offer incense before the LORD, to serve in his presence, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever.

**14** As for Moses, the man of God — his descendants were simply counted among the tribe of Levi.

**15** Moses' sons: Gershom and Eliezer.

**16** Gershom's descendants: Shebuel was the leader.

**17** Eliezer's descendants: Rehabiah was the leader. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's descendants became very numerous.

**18** Izhar's descendants: Shelomith was the leader.

**19** Hebron's sons: Jeriah (the leader), Amariah (second), Jahaziel (third), and Jekameam (fourth).

**20** Uzziel's sons: Micah (the leader) and Isshiah (second).

**21** Merari's sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons: Eleazar and Kish.

**22** Eleazar died without sons — he had only daughters. Their relatives, the sons of Kish, married them.

**23** Mushi's sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth — three.

**24** These were the descendants of Levi listed by their family groups — the heads of families registered by name and counted individually. They were twenty years old and above, and they performed the work of serving in the LORD's house.

**25** For David had said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given his people rest, and he has come to dwell in Jerusalem permanently.

**26** The Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all the equipment used in its service."

**27** According to David's final instructions, the Levites were counted from age twenty and above.

**28** Their job was to assist Aaron's descendants in the service of the LORD's house: maintaining the courtyards and side rooms, purifying everything that was holy, and performing the work required in God's house.

**29** They were responsible for the sacred bread set out in rows, the flour for grain offerings, the unleavened wafers, the baked goods, the offerings mixed with oil, and all measurements of quantity and size.

**30** They were also to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and again every evening.

**31** They assisted whenever burnt offerings were presented to the LORD — on Sabbaths, at New Moon festivals, and at all appointed feasts — always in the proper numbers, following the regulations prescribed for them as their constant duty before the LORD.

**32** In this way they fulfilled their responsibilities for the tent of meeting, the holy place, and the service of their relatives, the descendants of Aaron, in the house of the LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — The quiet succession:** "When David was old and had lived a full life, he made Solomon king." This is the Chronicler's serene version of what in 1 Kings 1 is a palace coup — Adonijah's rebellion, Bathsheba's intervention, Nathan's scheming. None of that appears here. In Chronicles, the transition is orderly, peaceful, divinely ordained. The Chronicler's David dies as he lived: organizing.

**Verse 13 — Aaron vs. Moses:** This verse draws a line that defines Israel's worship for a millennium. Aaron and his sons are "set apart for the most sacred duties" — incense, ministry, blessing. Moses' descendants? Verse 14 delivers the quiet verdict: "simply counted among the tribe of Levi." The greatest leader in Israel's history produces a line of ordinary Levites. The greatest priest produces an eternal priesthood. In the Chronicler's world, liturgical function outranks prophetic legacy.

**Verse 25-27 — Why lower the age?:** David's reasoning is practical and theological. The Levites were originally counted from age thirty (Numbers 4:3) because they needed to carry the heavy tabernacle. But now God "has come to dwell in Jerusalem permanently" — the tabernacle era is over. A permanent temple needs more workers, not fewer, and younger men can serve because the carrying is done. Administration replaces transportation.

*— PNEUMA*
